  "text": "Martin found the spare key in a tin of buttons, though his mother had insisted it was under the sink.

“That’s where it used to be,” she said.

He held up the tin.

“Well, you found it.”

The key was for the shed. A couple from the next village were coming to collect his father’s bicycle, and Martin had promised to pump the tyres.

Outside, the grass soaked the edges of his shoes. His mother watched from the kitchen window until he raised a hand, then turned away.

The shed door caught on the ground. He lifted it by the handle, as his father had, and squeezed through.

The bicycle stood behind a folded deckchair. On its handlebars hung a carrier bag containing three punctured inner tubes, each neatly tied.

Martin wheeled it onto the path.

His mother opened the back door.

“They’ll need the lights.”

“Are they in there?”

“Top drawer. Unless he moved them.”

The front light worked. The rear one didn’t. Martin unscrewed the casing and found a white crust around the batteries.

“I can get new ones,” he said.

“They said they’d come at four.”

“It’s only half past two.”

His mother came down the path carrying a yellow duster. She wiped the saddle, then the crossbar.

“He used to ride to the reservoir.”

“I know.”

“Not always. Sometimes he only went to the shop.”

She threaded the duster between the spokes. Martin steadied the wheel.

When she had finished, he put the dead batteries in his pocket.

“Anything you need while I’m out?”

She considered.

“Milk. The small one.”"
